name: Ten Yard Fight
label: Equal Vision
lede: Anthony Moreschi played Ten Yard Fight's first show in football gear, the band fired a guitarist for wanting to stop singing about football, and its last show, on a Boston Sunday with the playoffs next door at Fenway, turned into straight edge's own holiday.

eras.title: A joke in shoulder pads
eras.text: Ten Yard Fight started close to a joke: a straight edge band with a football theme and a singer in pads. The joke sold 1,000 demos and a 7" that was gone in under a week, and the band started taking itself seriously, some members more than others.

years.cap: Flyer: Ten Yard Fight with Floorpunch, Roswell, Fastbreak and Rancor, First Parish Church, Harvard Square, Boston, June 1, 1996
years.h: Moreschi plays Ten Yard Fight's first show in football gear
years.p: Singer Anthony "Wrench" Moreschi wears a mix of football gear and punk clothes, with John LaCroix on bass. Wikipedia gives no date for it.
years.xp:
The costume was the band's whole pitch: Wikipedia says Ten Yard Fight began as a straight edge band with a football theme. Anthony Pappalardo later objected to exactly that, and was gone within the year.

The flyer is from a Harvard Square church show the following June, with Floorpunch and Fastbreak on the same bill.

years.h: A Salad Days demo moves 1,000 copies
years.p: Ten Yard Fight record Demo '95 in October 1995 at Salad Days Studio. Bridge 9 and Wikipedia both say it sells 1,000 copies, a real number for a new Boston hardcore band.

years.h: Hardcore Pride is gone in under a week
years.p: The debut 7", recorded in March 1996 at Salad Days with [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]], comes out on Boston's Big Wheel Recreation. Wikipedia says the first pressing sells out in less than a week.

years.cap: Flyer: Fastbreak, 97a, Ten Yard Fight and Blade Crasher at the Basement, Sunday, Aug. 4, 1996
years.h: A split with Fastbreak, then a deal with Equal Vision
years.p: Ten Yard Fight and [[Fastbreak|6ca65199-3330-4cb6-8589-f57930d60c28]] share a 7". The noise around Hardcore Pride brings Equal Vision to the door.

years.big: "They told people I couldn't play guitar. That would be really hard to suck at."
years.h: Anthony Pappalardo is called to practice and fired there
years.p: Pappalardo wanted Ten Yard Fight to stop writing about football and bragging about straight edge. He told No Echo the band had him come to practice, then let him go.
years.xp:
His case, in his words to No Echo: "We need to stop singing about football." He wanted the songs to say why the band was edge, something actually positive. He also asked why a football band was wearing basketball jerseys.

Within two months he and singer Sweet Pete had started [[In My Eyes|f8a4cb28-0443-48af-b58a-b2b2ab51206d]], with rules: no old band shirts, no X imagery, and no straight edge songs.

He also rejected the youth crew revival tag, saying the band drew on [[Samiam|787aa69f-f419-4e24-8c13-33511a20428d]], [[Turning Point|19b7cbc9-0898-400a-87d5-bfa47c87487c]] and [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] as much as [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]].

eras.title: Revival, and a revolving door
eras.text: In 1997 Ten Yard Fight, In My Eyes and Floorpunch brought back the late-'80s youth crew sound, and Equal Vision put out the record that led the charge. The band toured the US and Europe hard while the line-up kept turning over.

years.h: Equal Vision's first Ten Yard Fight release is a catch-up CD
years.p: Hardcore Pride collects the 7" songs, Demo '95 and a cover of Brotherhood on one disc.

yt: Back on Track, live in Corona, CA, 1997
years.h: Back on Track lands on Equal Vision
years.p: Moreschi, guitarist Chris Patterson, bassist John LaCroix and drummer Ben Chused cut it in March 1997 at Salad Days with Brian McTernan. It spearheads the 1997 youth crew revival.
years.xp: The clip is the title track live at the Showcase in Corona, California, in 1997, taken from the band's own video The Only Way and posted by LaCroix.

years.cap: Flyer: Yuletide Hardcore Festival, 180 Club, Hagerstown, Maryland, Dec. 14, 1997, with Floorpunch, Ensign, Fastbreak, Bane and 10 Yd Fight
years.src: Discogs: Back on Track · Wikipedia: Bane
yt: Hardcore Pride, live at The Rat, Boston, Sept. 14, 1997
years.h: Converge's Aaron Dalbec plays second guitar live
years.p: The Back on Track credits list Dalbec, of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] and [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]], as Ten Yard Fight's live second guitarist. Drummer Ben Chused plays in Bane from 1997 to 1998.
years.xp: The flyer puts Bane and 10 Yd Fight on the same Maryland bill that December. The clip is Hardcore Pride live at The Rat in Boston on September 14, 1997.

years.h: Two years on the road, and the line-up turns over
years.p: Ten Yard Fight tour Europe and the US through 1997 and 1998. By the end Tim Cossar is on guitar, John LaCroix has moved from bass to guitar, and Brian "Clevo" Ristau plays bass.
years.xp: The Germany clip is Hardcore Pride from the 1998 European tour, also from the band's own video The Only Way.

years.h: Six songs at Impact Studios in Gloucester
years.p: Dean Baltulonis and Matt Henderson produce the November and December 1998 sessions in Gloucester, Massachusetts.

eras.title: Game day on Lansdowne Street
eras.text: Ten Yard Fight ended on a Boston Sunday with their friends on the bill and a playoff game at Fenway down the street. The date became a holiday.

years.h: The Only Way is the last record
years.p: Equal Vision issues it as EVR 49, the final line-up's only record. The CD adds a seventh song, No Place, that the 7" leaves off.

years.big: "I think we did way more than we ever set out to do, so I don't feel like we ended too soon."
years.src: Wikipedia: National Edge Day · Bridge 9 · No Echo: Anthony Moreschi
years.h: The last show, billed as Edge Fest, becomes Edge Day
years.p: Ten Yard Fight play the Karma Club on Lansdowne Street, beside Fenway Park, on a day of the American League Championship Series. Anthony Moreschi said that of the end afterward.
years.xp:
[[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]], Reach the Sky, In My Eyes and [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]] shared the bill, according to Wikipedia's National Edge Day page. It counts the night as the first National Edge Day and says it "marked the end of the 1990s 'youth crew' revival."

Straight edge kids now mark it every year, from Atlanta and Santa Ana to Gothenburg, London and Kuala Lumpur.

Moreschi filmed the show himself. He told No Echo it was his first real video project.

years.h: A home-video history closes the run
years.p: Bridge 9 puts out The Only Way: 1995-1999 in 2000, built around the final show, as the band's last release.

years.src: Wikipedia · The Punk Rock MBA · No Echo: Anthony Moreschi
years.h: Tim Cossar starts American Nightmare; John LaCroix starts a magazine
years.p: Anthony Moreschi moves to Southern California and later fronts Stand and Fight on Bridge 9. LaCroix and the band's roadie, Roger Gastman, start the art magazine While You Were Sleeping.
years.xp:
LaCroix and Gastman later started Swindle with Shepard Fairey. LaCroix went on to be a creative director, including on the NFL's first-down-line graphics, and played in Unrestrained.

Wikipedia also credits LaCroix with the first documented 'edge confession' letter, written after he broke edge sometime between 2000 and 2005.

eras.title: Edge Day, every year
eras.text: The band that gave straight edge its holiday kept turning up for it: Moreschi and Ristau as First and Ten, a reunion set at This Is Hardcore in 2018, and a yes to Furnace Fest in 2025.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight's singer and bassist play the holiday their last show started
years.p: Anthony Moreschi and Brian Ristau, billed as First and Ten, play National Edge Day 2007 in Haverhill, Massachusetts.

years.h: First and Ten and Slapshot share a bill
years.p: Moreschi and Ristau's First and Ten, Ten Yard Fight in all but name, play on November 8, 2008 with Boston's [[Slapshot|efc798e2-3165-49fd-a83b-d659cdb20488]].

years.h: The original line-up reunites to headline This Is Hardcore
years.p: Ten Yard Fight take the first day of This Is Hardcore 2018 in Philadelphia, and hate5six films the full set.

years.h: Moreschi turns filmmaker with Don't Stand in Line
years.p: Emmy-winning filmmaker Anthony Moreschi makes a six-part series on carrying DIY ethics from hardcore, BMX and skating into a career. The cast includes Bridge 9's Chris Wrenn and hate5six's Sunny Singh.
years.xp:
The other two subjects are Greg Walsh of Wolf Brigade Gym and Steve Crandall of FBM Bike Company. Moreschi shot it as a one-man crew on a small budget, keeping locations within driving distance of friends.

His line for the theme: "DIY until you die" is what you say young, and these four kept it going 25 years or more.

years.h: Furnace Fest books Ten Yard Fight after almost thirty years
years.p: Announced on February 14, 2025 alongside A Change of Pace, the set in Birmingham, Alabama is billed by Lambgoat as the band's return.
